title: Surjectivity descends to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $0\in I$ and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S_0$, where $S_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$ to $S_i$ and $f:X\to Y$ its base change to $S$ (fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]). If $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $f_i$ is surjective for some $i\ge0$ (Stacks Limits, Lemma 07RR).

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069), in Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property, line 1739); its proof: $f_0$ is of finite presentation, so $E=f_0(X_0)$ is constructible (Chevalley, Morphisms Lemma Tag 054J); the image of $f_i$ is the inverse image of $E$ in $Y_i$; $Y\to Y_0$ maps into $E$, so Limits Lemma Tag 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible) gives $i$ with $Y_i\to Y_0$ mapping into $E$

proof.text: *Step 1 (the image $E$ of $f_0$ is constructible).* Since $X_0$ is quasi-compact and $Y_0$ is quasi-separated, $f_0$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1); it is locally of finite presentation by hypothesis, and $Y_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Hence by [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] (clause $C=X_0$) the set $E=f_0(X_0)$ is a constructible subset of $Y_0$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. (Stacks says '$f_0$ is of finite presentation'; only quasi-compactness of $f_0$ and the hypotheses on $Y_0$ enter Chevalley's theorem.)

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069): 'The morphism $f_0$ is of finite presentation. Hence $E=f_0(X_0)$ is a constructible subset of $Y_0$, see Morphisms, Lemma 054J'

proof.text: *Step 2 ($f_T$ is the base change of $f_0$ along $Y_T\to Y_0$).* Let $u:T\to S_0$ be one of the morphisms $f_{i0}:S_i\to S_0$ ($i\ge0$) or the projection $S\to S_0$, and write $g_0:Y_0\to S_0$ for the structure morphism of $Y_0$, so that $g_0\circ f_0$ is that of $X_0$. Put $Y_T=Y_0\times_{S_0}T$ with projections $q_T:Y_T\to Y_0$, $g_T:Y_T\to T$, and $X_T=X_0\times_{S_0}T$ with projections $p_T:X_T\to X_0$, $h_T:X_T\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; the base change $f_T=f_0\times\mathrm{id}_T:X_T\to Y_T$ is the morphism with $q_T\circ f_T=f_0\circ p_T$ and $g_T\circ f_T=h_T$ (so $f_T=f_i$ for $T=S_i$ and $f_T=f$ for $T=S$). In the diagram with upper square $(X_T\xrightarrow{p_T}X_0,\ f_T,\ f_0,\ Y_T\xrightarrow{q_T}Y_0)$ and lower square $(Y_T\xrightarrow{q_T}Y_0,\ g_T,\ g_0,\ T\xrightarrow{u}S_0)$ both squares commute, the lower square is cartesian by definition of $Y_T$, and the outer rectangle $(X_T\xrightarrow{p_T}X_0,\ g_T\circ f_T=h_T,\ g_0\circ f_0,\ u)$ is cartesian by definition of $X_T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the upper square is cartesian: $(X_T,p_T,f_T)$ is a fibre product of $f_0$ and $q_T$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069): 'Since $f_i$ is the base change of $f_0$ by $Y_i\to Y_0$' (the pasting of fibre products, which the source leaves implicit, written out)

proof.text: *Step 3 (the image of $f_T$ is $q_T^{-1}(E)$).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] to the fibre product $(X_T,p_T,f_T)$ of $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ and $q_T:Y_T\to Y_0$ from Step 2, with $C=X_0$: $f_T(X_T)=f_T(p_T^{-1}(X_0))=q_T^{-1}(f_0(X_0))=q_T^{-1}(E)$. In particular $f_i(X_i)=q_{S_i}^{-1}(E)$ for every $i\ge0$ and $f(X)=q_S^{-1}(E)$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069): 'we see that the image of $f_i$ is the inverse image of $E$ in $Y_i$' (Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 01S1, line 1489: $q^{-1}(f(Z))=f_{S'}(p^{-1}(Z))$)

proof.text: *Step 4 ($Y\to Y_0$ maps into $E$).* Since $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], Step 3 for $T=S$ gives $Y=f(X)=q_S^{-1}(E)$, i.e. $q_S(Y)\subseteq E$ for the projection $q_S:Y=Y_0\times_{S_0}S\to Y_0$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069): 'Moreover, we know that $Y\to Y_0$ maps into $E$'

proof.text: *Step 5 ($Y$ is the limit of the system $(Y_i)_{i\ge0}$ of quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms).* Write $Y_i=Y_{S_i}=Y_0\times_{S_0}S_i$ for $i\ge0$, with transition morphisms $y_{ii'}=\mathrm{id}_{Y_0}\times f_{ii'}:Y_i\to Y_{i'}$ ($i\ge i'\ge0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] (with $T=Y_0$ and the structure morphism $g_0$) this is an inverse system over the directed set $I_{\ge0}=\{i\in I: i\ge0\}$ with affine transition morphisms, and $Y=Y_0\times_{S_0}S$ with the morphisms $\mathrm{id}_{Y_0}\times f_i:Y\to Y_i$ is its limit in the category of schemes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Under the canonical identification $Y_{S_0}=Y_0\times_{S_0}S_0=Y_0$ (via $q_{S_0}$, an isomorphism since $\mathrm{id}_{S_0}$ is), the transition morphism $y_{i0}$ is $q_{S_i}$ and the limit projection $Y\to Y_0$ is $q_S$. Each $q_{S_i}:Y_i\to Y_0$ is the base change of the affine morphism $f_{i0}$, hence affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (1), (3); since $Y_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so is $Y_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2).

source.place: Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property, line 1739) and Lemma Tag 01YZ (lemma-scheme-over-limit); the source applies Lemma Tag 05F4, stated in Situation Tag 086P (situation-descent, line 388: qcqs schemes, affine transition morphisms), to the system $(Y_i)$ without comment

proof.text: *Step 6 (a stage mapping into $E$).* By Step 5 the system $(Y_i,y_{ii'})_{i\ge0}$ over $I_{\ge0}$ with limit $(Y,(\mathrm{id}_{Y_0}\times f_i)_i)$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible]; take its index $0$, the constructible subset $E\subseteq Y_0$ of Step 1, and the inclusion $q_S(Y)\subseteq E$ of Step 4. It gives $i_1\ge0$ with $q_{S_i}(Y_i)=y_{i0}(Y_i)\subseteq E$ for every $i\ge i_1$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069): 'Hence we win by Lemma 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible, line 530)'

proof.text: *Step 7 (conclusion).* Let $i=i_1$. By Step 3 and Step 6, $f_i(X_i)=q_{S_i}^{-1}(E)=Y_i$, so $f_i$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] (and so is $f_{i'}$ for every $i'\ge i_1$).

split_report.summary: Split in seven steps along Stacks' proof of Limits 07RR, checked against limits.tex line 2069 and the cited lemmas. Step 1: f_0 quasi-compact (qcqs-morphism-permanence (1)), so E = f_0(X_0) is constructible by Chevalley (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image = Scheme.Hom.isConstructible_image, FinitePresentation.lean:165, @[stacks 054J], with IsConstructible.univ). Step 2: X_T -> Y_T is a fibre product of f_0 and Y_T -> Y_0 by pasting (reviewed leaf lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting), for T = S_i or S. Step 3: image of f_T = inverse image of E (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image = Scheme.image_preimage_eq_of_isPullback, PullbackCarrier.lean:420; the identity in the proof of Morphisms 01S1). Step 4: surjectivity of f gives Y -> Y_0 into E. Step 5: Y = lim Y_i with affine transitions (lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit, 01YZ) and Y_i qcqs (affine-morphism-permanence, qcqs-morphism-permanence (2)), the hypotheses of 05F4. Step 6: 05F4 (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible, stated for constructible E in Situation 086P; not in Mathlib, only the open case exists_map_eq_top). Step 7: conclusion. Statement kept; 05F3 not created (only cited in the source place of the 05F4 node, as part of Stacks' proof).
